issues.legal_issue: Registered sale deeds may be considered in determining compensation without their contents being proved by examining the buyer or seller.
material_facts: The claimants submitted registered sale deeds as evidence of the value of land near the acquired land.
The acquiring respondents did not challenge the authenticity of those documents.
The lower courts excluded most of the sale deeds because the buyer and seller had not been examined.
issues.conclusion: The lower courts could not discard the registered sale deeds on that ground; the deeds could be considered as evidence in determining compensation.
issues.legal_principle: Section 51-A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 permits registered sale documents to be received as evidence of the transactions recorded in them. The Court relied on Land Acquisition Officer and Mandal Revenue Officer v. V. Narasaiah, Cement Corporation of India v. Purya, and Deputy Collector, Land Acquisition, Gujarat v. Madhubai Gobarbhai.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_case: The proceeding concerns determination of compensation for compulsorily acquired land.
predicates.sale_deeds_are_registered: The claimant submitted registered documents recording land-sale transactions.
predicates.authenticity_is_unchallenged: The acquiring party did not challenge the authenticity of the registered sale documents.

issues.definition: When a compensation proceeding concerns acquired land and the submitted sale deeds are registered and their authenticity is not challenged, those deeds may be considered as evidence.

issues.legal_issue: When several comparable sale transactions are available, the highest bona fide exemplar should generally be preferred over averaging the transactions.
material_facts: Several sale deeds related to land transactions before the acquisition and were submitted to establish market value.
The highest-priced transactions were not shown to be collusive, fictitious, or otherwise not genuine.
The Court relied on the highest-priced exemplars when determining the compensation rate.
issues.conclusion: The Court adopted the highest bona fide sale exemplars rather than averaging the available sale prices.
issues.legal_principle: A bona fide highest exemplar among sales of similar land should generally be used; averaging is not appropriate where transaction values differ markedly. The Court relied on M. Vijayalakshmamma Rao Bahadur v. Collector, State of Punjab v. Hans Raj, Anjani Molu Dessai v. State of Goa, Mehrawal Khewaji Trust v. State of Punjab, and Chindha Fakira Patil v. Special Land Acquisition Officer.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_case: The proceeding concerns determination of compensation for compulsorily acquired land.
predicates.multiple_comparable_sales_exist: The parties placed more than one sale transaction involving comparable land before the court.
predicates.highest_comparable_sale_is_bona_fide: The highest-priced comparable transaction is genuine and is not shown to be collusive or otherwise unreliable.

issues.definition: If a compensation proceeding involves multiple comparable sales and the highest-priced sale is bona fide, that sale is preferred in assessing market value.

issues.legal_issue: Development-cost deductions are not justified where land is acquired for a railway line and no development work of the kind supporting the deductions is required or shown.
material_facts: The land was acquired for construction of a railway line.
The lower courts deducted amounts for land allegedly needed for roads, drains, sewer lines, parks, and electricity lines, and for development expenses.
The acquiring respondents produced no evidence that such development work was required for the railway line.
issues.conclusion: The deductions for development charges and development costs were legally unsustainable.
issues.legal_principle: The purpose of acquisition is relevant to whether development deductions are appropriate; development deductions do not arise merely by treating the acquired land as a site requiring a layout and amenities where the acquisition is for railway construction and no such development is required. The Court relied on Nelson Fernandes v. Special Land Acquisition Officer and C.R. Nagaraja Shetty v. Special Land Acquisition Officer, applying the principle in Viluben Jhalejar Contractor v. State of Gujarat.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_case: The proceeding concerns determination of compensation for compulsorily acquired land.
predicates.acquisition_is_for_railway_construction: The land was acquired for construction of a railway line rather than for development into plots or a built-up layout.
predicates.no_required_development_is_shown: The acquiring party did not show that roads, utilities, or other development work were required for the stated acquisition purpose.

issues.definition: Where land is acquired for railway construction and no required development work is shown, development-cost deductions are not justified.

issues.legal_issue: A deduction may be made to account for the size difference between small sale plots and a substantially larger acquired parcel.
material_facts: The acquired parcels were large in comparison with the small plots covered by the sale deeds used as exemplars.
The Court rejected deductions for development costs but approved a deduction based on the small size of the exemplar plots.
issues.conclusion: A deduction based on the smallness of the sale plots was permissible when determining compensation for the larger acquired parcels.
issues.legal_principle: Comparable-sale valuation requires adjustment for differences between the exemplar and acquired land, including the disadvantage of a large area compared with small plots. The Court relied on the adjustment factors stated in Viluben Jhalejar Contractor v. State of Gujarat.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_case: The proceeding concerns determination of compensation for compulsorily acquired land.
predicates.comparable_sale_plots_are_small: The sale transactions used as comparables concern plots substantially smaller than the acquired land.
predicates.acquired_parcel_is_large: The acquired land comprises a substantially larger parcel than the comparable sale plots.

issues.definition: When small sale plots are used to value a large acquired parcel in a compensation proceeding, a deduction to account for that size difference is permissible.

issues.legal_issue: The enhancement of compensation cannot exceed the rate claimed when the claimant limited the claim to that rate and did not seek a higher award in the appellate proceedings.
material_facts: The Court's valuation analysis supported a rate higher than the rate claimed before the reference court.
The claimants had limited their claim to a lower rate and made no application in the High Court or Supreme Court seeking compensation at a higher rate.
issues.conclusion: The Court restricted the enhanced compensation to the rate the claimants had claimed.
issues.legal_principle: Although the evidence and valuation principles may support a higher market value, the Court restricted relief to the claim actually pursued because no higher compensation had been sought in the appellate proceedings.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal seeking increased compensation for acquired land.
predicates.claimant_limited_the_compensation_claim: The claimant expressly confined the compensation sought to a particular rate before the reference court.
predicates.no_higher_claim_was_pursued_on_appeal: The claimant did not apply in the appellate proceedings for compensation at a rate above the amount originally claimed.

issues.definition: In a compensation appeal, if the claimant limited the original claim and pursued no higher claim on appeal, the enhancement is limited to the claimed rate.

issues.legal_issue: Interest is payable on the solatium component of compensation for acquired land.
material_facts: The claimants were entitled to solatium as part of the compensation for their acquired land.
They sought interest on the solatium component.
issues.conclusion: The claimants were entitled to interest on solatium.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Sunder v. Union of India, Chimanlal Kuberdas Modi v. Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation, Nadirsha Shapurji Patel v. Collector and Land Acquisition Officer, R. Saragapani v. Special Tahsildar, and Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited v. R.S. Avtar Singh and Company, holding that interest is payable on solatium.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_case: The proceeding concerns compensation for compulsorily acquired land.
predicates.solatium_is_awarded: The owner is awarded solatium as part of the compensation for the acquired land.

issues.definition: When solatium is awarded in a compensation proceeding for acquired land, interest is payable on that solatium.
